citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518

isBasedOn.name: Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering

abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: The gate binds every threshold arm, including the single verifier and the equal-weight pool.
Validator compute is not equal across arms, so an equal candidate budget does not mean equal assessment cost.
